citation.title: Design and Testing of Honeycomb Sandwich Cylinders Under Axial Compression
citation.authors: John H. Cunningham and Marcus J. Jacobson (Douglas Aircraft Co.)
citation.report_no: NASA TN D-1510 (Collected Papers on Instability of Shell Structures, NASA symposium 24-25 Oct 1962); paper pp. 341-359 as printed

access: full text (OCR PDF, tables checked against page image)

geometry.R: outside diameter 36 in (mean radius not stated)
geometry.note: 8 cylinders tested; first 3 failed at low stress from unscalloped end doublers (paper: stress below ~30,000 psi); 5 satisfactory cylinders reported in Table I

faces.note: stress-strain curve from tension coupons (compression coupons not feasible); Fig. 11

core.type: Hexcel aluminium honeycomb, 3/16-5052-.001P, ribbon direction parallel to load
core.G_c: 20,000 and 40,000 psi were the values used in the predictions (axial shear modulus; 40,000 on Fig. 4 legend)
core.G_c_direction: plane normal to faces and parallel to load
core.missing: core density; measured G_c not given

prediction_basis: Small-deflection classical sandwich-cylinder buckling WITH core shear (rigid-core region, Eq. 1-2) with a tangent-modulus plasticity reduction (stress at intersection of K*Et curve and tension stress-strain curve, Fig. 7-10); large-deflection (postbuckling) theory; symmetric-wrinkling and monocell criteria. No imperfections assumed. Predictions are in the inelastic range, so they are plasticity-reduced values, not elastic classical stresses.
ratios_note: No measured/predicted ratio is stated. The paper says the 0.010 in faces were stabilised well into the inelastic range and failures occurred at stresses much higher than predicted by large-deflection theory; it says small-deflection general-instability and wrinkling predictions are in close agreement with each other and that exact agreement with test is not expected. Raw numbers above are as printed; no ratios computed here.

locations.item: Table I (loads, face stress, failure type)
locations.quote: Wrinkle About 6" from End

locations.item: Table II (predicted vs actual failing stress)
locations.quote: Predicted Buckling Stresses (psi) ... Actual Failing Stress (Psi)
eight 7075-T6 aluminum sandwich cylinders with faces 0.010 inches thick
failures occurred at stresses much higher than predicted by the large deflection theory

missing_inputs: E_f measured; core density; measured G_c; mean R; Poisson ratio
stress-strain data are tension, not compression (paper says so)
caveat: Tests are in the plastic range with plasticity-reduced predictions. NASA CR-1457 Sec. 4.2.1.2.1 explicitly warns that comparing inelastic test stress against an inelastic prediction hides the true knockdown (compare to the elastic classical value). Failure was local face wrinkling at/near stress levels of the wrinkling prediction, not clean general instability. Thin faces: R/t_f is large, but the stated imperfection discussion says imperfection sensitivity is tied to total sandwich thickness.

citation.title: Buckling of Layered Orthotropic and Sandwich Cylindrical Shells in Axial Compression
citation.authors: Edward W. Kuenzi (U.S. Forest Products Laboratory)
citation.report_no: NASA TN D-1510 symposium paper, pp. 323-330 as printed (NASA Symposium on Instability of Shell Structures, 24-25 Oct 1962)

access: full text (OCR PDF); Fig. 3-4 read from page image

shell.type: curved sandwich panels treated as representing a complete cylinder (calculation: panels larger than one theoretical buckle); the paper says further experiments on complete sandwich cylinders are needed

geometry.missing: panel dimensions and radius are in FPL Report 1830 (ref. 6 of the paper), which was not opened

core.type: end-grain balsa wood and soft cork board (not honeycomb or foam)
core.G_c: range 320 psi to 15,000 psi (core modulus of rigidity)

measured: Experimental facing stresses at buckling were converted to an experimental N (non-dimensional buckling coefficient) via formula (7); plotted vs theoretical N in Fig. 4 (approximately 30-40 symbols, count not stated; not tabulated). Facing stresses at buckling were well below compressive proportional limit (elastic).
prediction_basis: Large-deflection (von Karman-Tsien diamond-mode) theory modified for sandwich with core shear by an approximate 'tilting' method (March and Kuenzi, FPL 1830). N=1 at V=0 is the shear-rigid-core limit. This is NOT the small-deflection classical stress.
ratios_as_stated: Qualitative: 'reasonably close agreement between experimental and theoretical values of N'. No numeric ratio. Figure 4: most points lie on the soft-core (low N, <0.4) part; two points near N about 1.0-1.1 lie slightly above the 45 degree line (eye-read, approximate).

locations.quote: there is reasonably close agreement between experimental and theoretical values of N
Core modulus of rigidity values ranged from 15,000 psi. to 320 psl.
Further experimental evaluation of complete sandwich cylindrical shells is necessary.

missing_inputs: panel geometry, face thickness and E, core thickness, density, individual test values (all in FPL 1830, unread)
caveat: These are the data CR-1457 re-plots as 'ref 4-2'. NASA CR-1457 Fig. 4.2-3 shows two stiff-core points from ref 4-2 at R/rho about 1050 and 1300 with gamma_c about 0.42-0.44 (eye-read), consistent with experiment equal to large-deflection theory, i.e. about 0.4 of the small-deflection value.

citation.title: Structural Behavior and Buckling Strength of Honeycomb Sandwich Cylinders Subjected to Bending
citation.authors: James P. Peterson and James Kent Anderson (NASA Langley)

access: full text (OCR PDF with spaced letters; key tables and Figs. 2, 9 checked on page images)

shell.loading: pure bending (the paper argues bending buckling load per unit circumference is little different from compression)

geometry.R: diameter about 77 in (1.96 m) => R about 38.5 in (unit arithmetic only); R/h = 157, 117, 92 for cylinders 1, 2, 3
geometry.note: scalloped doublers at both ends; six longitudinal splices per face sheet

faces.note: h/t_s = 11.6, 16.1, 21.5 (h = depth between face centroids); tension coupon stress-strain curves (Fig. 5), no compression curves

core.type: 3003-H19 aluminium hexagonal honeycomb, 1/4 in cell, 0.002 in foil, bonded with FM 47 Type II adhesive film (glass carrier)
core.G_c: G_xz taken from a plot of G_xz vs relative density (Fig. 3, from MIL-HDBK-23 data); no numeric value stated in text
core.missing: t_c not tabulated (only h/t_s and R/h); G_c numeric

prediction_basis: Plastic-buckling equation derived in the paper for isotropic sandwich cylinders with shear-resistant core (axisymmetric mode, small-deflection with transverse shear and plasticity; wall stiffnesses include core and adhesive contributions). Calculated N_calc uses stiffnesses at the calculated buckling load. Not the large-deflection MIL-HDBK-23 chart (which gives about 40 percent of this prediction for elastic shear-resistant-core cylinders).
ratios_as_stated: Fig. 9 plots N_test/N_calc vs R/rho. Eye-read (approximate): cyl 1 about 0.87 at R/rho about 300; cyl 2 about 0.92 at about 235; cyl 3 about 0.89 at about 190. Text: recomputing with stiffnesses at the TEST strain lowers the points by about 20 percent (cyl 3, most plastic) and about 6 percent (cyl 1); on that basis the cylinders buckled lower than the conventional-cylinder curve.
recommended_knockdown: None formal. Finding: sandwich bending cylinders fall on the NASA lower-limit curve for conventional thin-wall cylinders in bending (Peterson TN D-526 / ref 18), with early buckling attributed to prebuckling wall bending from end restraint (Poisson expansion).

locations.quote: Buckling of the test cylinders occurred at lower loads than predicted by theory

locations.location: printed p. 12 (table before 'Test Specimens and Test Procedure')

locations.quote: Correlation of buckling load of test cylinders with buckling data on conventional thin-wall cylinders.

locations.location: Results and Discussion, around printed pp. 15-16
locations.quote: lowered approximately 20 percent, the least plastic cylinder (cylinder 1) by approximately 6 percent

missing_inputs: tabulated N_test and N_calc values (only in Fig. 9)
caveat: Stresses at buckling are at or into the face-sheet inelastic range (plastic buckling equation), so N_test/N_calc is plasticity-adjusted, not an elastic classical knockdown. CR-1457 re-reduces these three cylinders to gamma_b (LITB-07) with different numbers. Elastic region ratios are therefore not directly given here.

citation.title: Test of a Truss-Core Sandwich Cylinder Loaded to Failure in Bending
citation.authors: James P. Peterson and James Kent Anderson (NASA Langley)
citation.report_no: NASA TN D-3157 (NTRS record lists date Dec 1, 1965; printed text signed Aug 19, 1965)

access: full text (OCR PDF; Figs. 1 and 12 checked on page images)

shell.type: circular cylinder, all-welded TRUSS-CORE (corrugated-core) sandwich - not honeycomb or foam

geometry.L: 31.25 in dimension labelled on Fig. 1 beside the test region (read as test-section length; not confirmed in text)
geometry.note: one cylinder; initial wall imperfections about one-half the wall thickness (average wall thickness 0.242 in)

faces.E_f: 31,500 ksi (stated as measured/tabulated Young's modulus of wall material); axial wall stiffness E_x = 1050 kips/in

core.type: corrugated truss core of Rene 41 sheet, web thickness 0.0070 in; section depth h = 0.242 in
core.G_c: transverse shear stiffness assumed large; a check using the weak (circumferential) direction changed the calculated buckling load by less than 1 percent

prediction_basis: Classical small-deflection buckling theory (eq. A4 of NACA TN 2601, Stein and Mayers) using measured axial wall stiffness and large shear stiffness; simply supported ends (clamped ends would raise it about 4 percent).
ratios_as_stated: Failure at about 62 percent of the classical small-deflection load, and about 80 percent of the design load (design used the NASA bending lower-bound correlation).
recommended_knockdown: None formal; the paper says the gap is comparable to extrapolating the lower limit of conventional thin-wall cylinder data.

locations.location: Summary, printed p. 1 and Test Results p. 6
locations.quote: Failure occurred at 62 percent of the calculated load
imperfections on the order of one-half the wall thickness are prevalent

missing_inputs: core density/G_c (not applicable in the honeycomb sense)
caveat: Not honeycomb or foam. Included as a documented sandwich-shell bending test with measured imperfections. The paper also says the earlier honeycomb cylinders of TN D-2926 agreed well with the NASA conventional-cylinder curve, while this one, with measurable buckle-like imperfections, fell near the lower limit of data from various sources (about 0.6 at its abscissa).

citation.title: Manual for Structural Stability Analysis of Sandwich Plates and Shells
citation.authors: R. T. Sullins, G. W. Smith, E. E. Spier (General Dynamics Convair, for NASA MSC, contract NAS 9-8244)

access: full text (OCR PDF; Figs. 4.2-3, 4.2-4, 4.2-5, 4.3-1 viewed as images; numbers read from plots are approximate eye-reads)

geometry.R: design variable; knockdown is a function of R/rho where rho = h/2 for equal faces (h = distance between facing middle surfaces)
geometry.L: not stated for the data set

faces.material: not tabulated for the underlying data

core.type: mixed (stiff-core data from honeycomb and plastic-faced cylinders; weak-core points from FPL panels)
core.G_c: G_xz and G_yz enter through V_c = sigma_o / sigma_crimp, sigma_crimp = (t1+t2) t_c G_xz / ... (Eq. 4.2-7, OCR garbled)

measured: Figure 4.2-3 plots 11 axial-compression sandwich cylinder points (non weak-core) plus 2 cone points as gamma_c vs R/rho: FPL 1830 (ref 4-2), Baker AIAA J. Sept 1968 (ref 4-10), Jenkinson and Kuenzi FPL PE-227 (ref 4-28). Eye-read gamma_c: ref 4-2: about 0.42 and 0.44 at R/rho about 1050 and 1300; ref 4-10 cylinders: about 0.54 (R/rho 180), 0.69, 0.58, 0.57 (about 270), 0.49 (about 410); ref 4-28: about 0.76, 0.63, 0.61 (R/rho about 105); ref 4-10 cones: about 0.57 and 0.51-0.52 (R/rho about 195). Numbers not tabulated.
prediction_basis: Classical small-deflection sandwich theory of Zahn and Kuenzi (FPL-018, 1963) with core shear, facing bending about own middle surface neglected; test points converted to elastic-equivalent (plasticity-corrected) stress before dividing (Sec. 4.2.1.2.1, Eqs. 4.2-12 to 4.2-15).
ratios_as_stated: gamma_c (test/classical) per Fig. 4.2-3 as above. Weak-core (V_c >= 2) panels from ref 4-2: Fig. 4.2-4 (about 40 points, test sigma_cr 3-17 ksi vs predicted 1-13 ksi) - 'all but one of the test results exceed the predicted strengths', the exception at 86 percent. One weak-core Hexcel (ref 4-11) test point (Fig. 4.2-5, test about 140 ksi vs predicted about 165 ksi, eye-read) appears to be that 86 percent point (inference from position; text does not say).
recommended_knockdown: Design gamma_c is the solid curve of Fig. 4.2-3, stated to be 75 percent of a curve derived from the Seide-Weingarten-Morgan isotropic lower bound (gamma = 1 - 0.901(1 - e^-phi)) rewritten in terms of R/rho. Eye-read values of the solid curve: about 0.68 at R/rho = 10, about 0.55 at 100, about 0.31 at 1000. All plotted test points lie on or above it (eye). Weak-core (V_c > 2, shear crimping): gamma = 1, no knockdown. Stiff or moderately stiff core (V_c < 2): curve above, stated to be only a 'best-available' approach. Transition for 0 < V_c < 2 not defined by a continuous relation.

locations.quote: Eleven such data points are shown.
gives gamma_c values that are 75 percent of those obtained from the dashed curve
all but one of the test results exceed the predicted strengths
the method proposed here is not very reliable when V_c < 2.0
lack of sufficient sandwich test data for a thorough empirical determination
some of the results presented in the literature can be quite misleading

missing_inputs: per-point geometry, face and core properties for refs 4-10, 4-28 (CR-1457 does not tabulate them); Baker AIAA 1968 and Hexcel 25 Jul 1963 status summary not opened
caveat: The 'recommended' curve is a design curve built mostly from isotropic-cylinder data plus a handful of sandwich points, scaled to 75 percent; it is not itself a measurement. Axis is R/rho, not R/t_f.

citation.title: Manual for Structural Stability Analysis of Sandwich Plates and Shells (Sec. 4.4.1.2, 'Empirical Knock-Down Factor', external lateral pressure)
citation.report_no: NASA CR-1457; underlying tests: (a) M. I. Kazimi, 'Sandwich Cylinders Part II - Uniformity of the Mechanical Properties of the Core', Aerospace Engineering, Sept 1960 (CR-1457 ref 4-27); (b) P. M. Jenkinson and E. W. Kuenzi, 'The Buckling Under External Radial Pressure and Buckling Under Axial Compression of Sandwich Cylindrical Shells', FPL Report PE-227, Jan 1962 (ref 4-28). Neither primary source opened.

access: full text of CR-1457 secondary summary only; primary reports not opened

geometry.note: not given in CR-1457; for ref 4-28, facings were thick, t_f/h about 0.25

faces.material: (a) not stated; (b) glass-reinforced plastic, three layers of glass fabric per facing, in-plane essentially isotropic

core.type: (a) honeycomb, one cylinder normal-expanded and one over-expanded core; (b) not stated in CR-1457

prediction_basis: Theoretical Pcr from MIL-HDBK-23 (CR-1457 ref 4-5) classical small-deflection sandwich theory with gamma_p = 1.0 (no knockdown). For cylinders 2-5 of ref 4-28 the paper reports initial buckling between 50 and 55 psi, so CR-1457 assumed 52.5 psi for each.
ratios_as_stated: Kazimi 0.56 and 0.88; Jenkinson-Kuenzi 1.00 to 1.16 (all at or above theory). Total 7 cylinders.
recommended_knockdown: Uniform gamma_p = 0.90 regardless of R/t, stated to follow SP-8007 (CR-1457 cites the Sept 1965 edition). CR-1457 calls the method 'best-available' and says more tests with small t_f/h are desirable. Note: the Kazimi normal-expanded result (0.56) is below 0.90; the report nevertheless says the results 'seem to provide added justification'.

locations.quote: uniform knock-down factor gamma_p of 0.90 regardless of the radius-to-thickness ratio
Normal-Expanded 17 30.5 .56 ; Over-Expanded 27 30.5 .88
initial buckling occurred at external lateral pressures which ranged from 50 to 55 psi
meager test data available from sandwich cylinders subjected to external lateral pressure

missing_inputs: geometry (R, L), face/core properties and G_c for all 7 cylinders (primary reports unread)
caveat: Only 7 cylinders, thick facings (t_f/h about 0.25) in one series; the one honeycomb series has two cylinders, scatter attributed by Kazimi to core uniformity. External-pressure buckling is less imperfection-sensitive for isotropic shells, which is the stated reason for 0.90.

citation.title: Manual for Structural Stability Analysis of Sandwich Plates and Shells (Chapters 5 and 6: cones, domes)
citation.report_no: NASA CR-1457; underlying: E. H. Baker AIAA J. Sept 1968 (ref 5-2, 4-10); North American Rockwell XSM-64A conical bulkhead tests (refs 5-7, 5-8); Gonzalez and Patton, S-II 55-inch domes (ref 6-4). Primary sources not opened.

shell.type: truncated cones (axial compression and hydrostatic) and sandwich domes (external pressure) - not cylinders
shell.loading: axial compression (cones); uniform external pressure (cone bulkhead, domes)

geometry.note: cones: vertex half-angle 15 degrees (two Baker cones); other geometry not given in CR-1457

measured: Cones, axial: two Baker cones, converted via equivalent-cylinder concept (R = radius at small end, L = slant length) to gamma_c about 0.5-0.6 (eye-read from Fig. 4.2-3, with the 'ref 4-10 conical' symbols). Cone hydrostatic: one North American Rockwell test specimen analysed, experimental 43.6 psi vs design critical pressure 36.4 psi (the second specimen stressed too far into plasticity and not analysed). Domes: 2 hemisphere and 6 approximately ellipsoidal dome points (some with thermal gradient) in Fig. 6.2-3; 3 specimens discarded as too plastic, 1 for faulty edge.
prediction_basis: Equivalent cylinder (cones); classical small-deflection with plasticity reduction (domes).
ratios_as_stated: Cone hydrostatic: 36.4 predicted vs 43.6 test (ratio not stated). Domes: gamma_d values only in Fig. 6.2-3, not tabulated.
recommended_knockdown: Domes under external pressure: gamma_d = 0.20 for hemispheres, 0.35 for ellipsoids and torispherical domes (Eqs. 6.2-13, 6.2-14), explicitly 'based on meager test results', rough guideline only. Cones: use equivalent-cylinder gamma_c.

citation.title: Buckling of Thin-Walled Circular Cylinders (NASA Space Vehicle Design Criteria, Structures), Sec. 4.4 Isotropic Sandwich Cylinders
citation.authors: V. I. Weingarten, P. Seide, J. P. Peterson

access: full text (OCR PDF, Aug 1968 revision); Fig. 11 viewed as image; plot values eye-read

geometry.R: abscissa is r/h (radius over sandwich depth between face centroids)

core.G_c: G_xz, G_yz enter through the parameter N_o/D_q

prediction_basis: Small-deflection sandwich buckling theory (NACA TN 2601; FPL-018 Zahn and Kuenzi) times a correlation factor gamma.
recommended_knockdown: Axial: gamma from Fig. 11 vs r/h, same functional form as isotropic cylinder with thickness replaced by geometric-mean radius of gyration; eye-read about 0.86 at r/h = 10, about 0.7 at 100, about 0.31 at 1000; the correction fades and reaches zero for a weak (shear-crimping) core (N_o/D_q > 2). Bending: Fig. 12. Lateral pressure: gamma = 0.56 with Fig. 13, 'no experimental data to substantiate'. Designs limited to delta >= 0.03 unless substantiated by tests.

locations.quote: Figures 9 and 10 are based on the small-deflection buckling theory

designs should be limited to sandwiches with rather heavy cores

caveat: Design guidance, not a measurement. CR-1457 cites SP-8007 (Sept 1965 edition) for a uniform 0.90 in external pressure, whereas the Aug 1968 revision text read here gives 0.56 with Fig. 13; I did not open the 1965 edition, so the difference is unresolved.
